messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — starting ~10:12 UTC we're seeing a spike in 429s for EU-west pools. Apps report short bursts, clients are retrying hard and causing cascading queue growth. Any quick ideas for client-level mitigations?

emma: Thanks for the flag. Do we have the exact response headers? Are these 429s carrying any backpressure hints (admit window, retry-after)?

sanjay: Pasting a sample response from the edge (copied from logs):

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Admit: refuse
X-RW-Admit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-Admit-Reset: 45
Retry-After: 2
{ "error": "capacity_exceeded" }

luke: OK, two high-level things for SDKs: 1) Respect Retry-After and the X-RW-* admit headers. 2) Switch to jittered exponential backoff with a capped window if X-RW-Admit-Reset is present. We'll draft a small patch.

kai: From infra side: EU-west pool hit a tight GPU maintenance window + a few noisy tenants. Autoscaler couldn't spin up fast enough because of AZ placement constraints. autoscale-bot shows a pending scale event around 10:10 that didn't finish until 10:18.

autoscale-bot: [notice] pending_scale: pool=euwest-gpu-64 type=add_nodes requested=8 state=provisioning eta=00:08:00

sanjay: We're seeing clients fallback to other regions but some apps don't want cross-region traffic. Are there graceful geo-fallback rules we can suggest?

emma: For latency-sensitive apps we recommend: prefer local region, then same-continent fallback, then global. SDK should expose a opt-in geo-fallback policy. Also honor any per-tenant "no-cross-region" flag returned from control plane.

luke: Proposal for SDK behavior (short):
1) On 429 with X-RW-Admit=refuse -> immediate backoff: base_delay = max( Retry-After (s), 0.5s )
2) If X-RW-Admit-Reset present -> treat as soft quota, avoid retries until reset, allow one after-reset probe every reset_interval/4
3) Add jitter +/- 30%
4) Expose config: fallback_regions=["eu-west-1","eu-central-1","us-east-1"] and honor tenant opt-outs

emma: Also add telemetry counters: admit_refuse_count, admit_probe_after_reset, geo_fallback_used. We need to correlate with per-pool GPU utilization.

kai: Ops action items: 1) Mark the noisy tenants and throttle at fleet edge for next 12h. 2) Eagerly provision extra nodes in euwest zone if node inventory allows. 3) Create temporary admission of X-RW-Admit: degrade for tolerant tenants to avoid global 429 cascade.

sanjay: Short-term client guidance we can publish: 1) Backoff on Retry-After and X-RW-Admit-Reset. 2) Use jittered exponential backoff. 3) Do not aggressive fanout to other regions — prefer controlled geo-fallback. 4) Add a probe policy instead of continuous retries.

luke: I'll open a tiny RFC + SDK PR with default behavior and opt-out knobs. Will include code snippet for interpreting headers: 
```js
const retryAfter = parseFloat(res.headers['retry-after'] || '0');
const admitReset = parseInt(res.headers['x-rw-admit-reset'] || '0', 10);
if (res.status === 429) {
  const base = Math.max(retryAfter, 0.5);
  const delay = jitteredExpBackoff(base, attempts, admitReset);
  await sleep(delay);
}
```

kai: I'll add a dashboard panel that surfaces X-RW-Admit counts and average admit-reset windows per pool, plus a short runbook.

emma: One more note — clients should also honor a new header we may add: X-RW-Available-GPUs to let autoscaling-aware SDKs make smarter decisions. Will prototype next week.

sanjay: Great. For now we'll post the short guidance in docs and patch SDK for parsing headers. Thanks all :thumbsup:
